A wastewater basin initially holds $⟦V⟧\,\text{L}$ of water containing $⟦q0⟧\,\text{kg}$ of dissolved pollutant.
A solution containing $⟦c⟧\,\text{kg/L}$ of dissolved pollutant is pumped into the basin at a rate of $⟦r⟧\,\text{L/min},$ while the completely mixed liquid is drained out at a rate of $⟦r⟧\,\text{L/min}.$ Which expression gives the amount of pollutant $Q(t),$ in kilograms, in the basin $t$ minutes after pumping begins?
17592186229724.solution_mask:
Let $Q$ be the amount of pollutant in the basin at time $t,$ in minutes. Then, the derivative 

$$
\frac{dQ}{dt}
$$

describes how this amount changes with respect to time $t.$ This is equal to the rate at which pollutant enters the basin minus the rate at which pollutant leaves the basin.

$$
\frac{dQ}{dt}={Q}_{\text{in}}^{′}-{Q}_{\text{out}}^{′}
$$

Note that the units of $\frac{dQ}{dt},{Q}_{\text{in}}^{′}$ and ${Q}_{\text{out}}^{′}$ are $\text{kg}/\text{min}.$ Now, let's compute the required rates of change in steps.

**Step 1**: Calculating the rate at which additives enter the basin.

Note that a feed solution containing $⟦c⟧\,\text{kg/L}$ of the pollutant enters the basin at a rate of $⟦r⟧\,\text{L/min}.$ So, the rate at which the *pollutant* enters the basin is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{Q}_{\text{in}}^{′} & =(⟦c⟧\,\frac{\text{kg}}{\text{L}})\cdot (⟦r⟧\,\frac{\text{L}}{\text{min}}) \\  & =(⟦c⟧\,\frac{\text{kg}}{\cancel{\text{L}}})\cdot (⟦r⟧\,\frac{\cancel{\text{L}}}{\text{min}}) \\  & =⟦F⟧\,\frac{\text{kg}}{\text{min}}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 2**: Calculating the rate at which additives exit the basin.

Next, note that the rate of flow in equals the rate of flow out, so the volume in the basin remains $⟦V⟧\,\text{L}.$ Then, since $Q$ is the amount of pollutant in the basin, the *concentration* of the solution at time $t$ is

$$
\frac{Q}{⟦V⟧}\,\text{kg/L}.
$$

Therefore, as the completely mixed liquid leaves at a rate of $⟦r⟧\,\text{L/min},$ *pollutant* leaves at a rate of

$$
\begin{aligned}{Q}_{\text{out}}^{′} & =(⟦r⟧\,\frac{\text{L}}{\text{min}})\cdot (\frac{Q}{⟦V⟧}\,\frac{\text{kg}}{\text{L}}) \\  & =(⟦r⟧\,\frac{\cancel{\text{L}}}{\text{min}})\cdot (\frac{Q}{⟦V⟧}\,\frac{\text{kg}}{\cancel{\text{L}}}) \\  & =\frac{⟦r⟧Q}{⟦V⟧}\,\frac{\text{kg}}{\text{min}} \\  & =\frac{Q}{25}\,\frac{\text{kg}}{\text{min}}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Calculate the overall rate of change.

The rate of change equals the rate of entry minus the rate of exit. Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dQ}{dt} & ={Q}_{\text{in}}^{′}-{Q}_{\text{out}}^{′} \\  & =⟦F⟧-\frac{Q}{25}\end{aligned}
$$

which gives the equation

$$
\frac{dQ}{dt}+\frac{1}{25}Q=⟦F⟧.
$$

**Step 4**: Integrate the equation.

This is a first-order linear equation with constant coefficients. To find the general solution, we must sum the complementary and particular solutions.

- To find the complementary solution ${Q}_{c},$ we solve the corresponding homogeneous equation, given by

$$
\frac{d{Q}_{c}}{dt}+\frac{1}{25}{Q}_{c}=0.
$$

Solving using an integration technique, such as separation of variables, we obtain the complementary solution

$$
{Q}_{c}(t)=A{e}^{-t/25},
$$

where $A$ is a constant of integration.

- Next, we find the particular solution. Note that the right-hand side of the inhomogeneous equation is a polynomial of degree $0.$ So, we assume that the particular solution is also a polynomial of degree $0,$ i.e.,

$$
{Q}_{p}(t)=\alpha .
$$

To find the value of $\alpha ,$ we substitute ${Q}_{p}=\alpha $ and $\frac{d{Q}_{p}}{dt}=(\alpha )^{′}=0$ into the inhomogeneous equation:

$$
0+\frac{1}{25}\alpha =⟦F⟧\,⟹\,\alpha =⟦E⟧.
$$

Therefore, the particular solution is ${Q}_{p}(t)=⟦E⟧.$

Now, since the general solution is given by the sum of the complementary solution and the particular solution, the general solution in our case is

$$
Q(t)={Q}_{c}(t)+{Q}_{p}(t)=A{e}^{-t/25}+⟦E⟧.
$$

We're told that the basin initially contains $⟦q0⟧\,\text{kg}$ of dissolved pollutant. So, we can apply the initial condition $Q(0)=⟦q0⟧,$ and solve for $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(0) & =⟦q0⟧ \\ A{e}^{-0/25}+⟦E⟧ & =⟦q0⟧ \\ A & =⟦B⟧\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain the following expression for $Q(t):$

$$
Q(t)=⟦E⟧-⟦absB⟧{e}^{-t/25}.
$$

$$

$$
\frac{Q}{⟦V⟧}\,\text{kg/L}.
$$

$$

$$

$$

$$

where $A$ is a constant of integration.

$$

$$

$$

$$

rounded to two decimal places.
